back_translation: Who is like the wise man? Who knows the explanation of things? A man's wisdom makes his face shine, and the hardness of his face is changed.
I advise: keep the king's command, because of the oath you have given before God.
Do not hurry to leave his presence, and do not persist in an evil matter, for he will do whatever he pleases.
For the king's word is supreme, and who can say to him, “What are you doing?”
Whoever keeps the command will meet no evil thing, and the heart of the wise knows both the proper time and the proper way.
For every matter has its proper time and way, even though man's misery weighs heavily upon him.
For no one knows what will happen — who can tell him when it will come to be?
No man has power over the wind to restrain the wind; no one has power over the day of his death; there is no discharge in time of war; and wickedness does not release those who practice it.
All this I saw when I gave my attention to every deed that is done under the sun: there is a time when one man exercises power over another to his own hurt.
Then I saw the wicked buried — those who used to come and go from the holy place — and they were forgotten in the city where they had done so. This too is without substance.
When the sentence against an evil deed is not carried out quickly, the hearts of the sons of men become filled with determination to do evil.
Though a sinner does evil a hundred times and still lives long, yet I know that it will be well with those who fear God, who fear before Him.
But it will not be well with the wicked man, and his days will not lengthen like a shadow, because he does not fear God.

There is something without substance that happens on the earth: there are righteous men who receive what fits the deeds of the wicked, and wicked men who receive what fits the deeds of the righteous. I said that this too is without substance.

So I commended joy, because under the sun there is nothing better for a man than to eat, to drink, and to rejoice; for this joy will stay with him in his toil through the days of his life that God has given him under the sun.
When I set my heart to know wisdom and to see the task that is done on the earth — though one's eyes see no sleep by day or by night —

then I saw all the work of God: that man is unable to fathom the work that is done under the sun. However hard a man toils to seek it out, he will not find it; and even if a wise man claims to know, he cannot fathom it.
